findings.reason: Both protected sources declare the explicitly prohibited local loop variable `index`. The inert candidate preserves the exact greedy adjacent-repair algorithm and app-local in-place contract while using the conventional interview variable `i`.

Apart from the prohibited name, the implementation is already the canonical optimal method: each position checks its required non-strict inequality and swaps only a violating adjacent pair. The candidate makes no algorithmic or micro-optimization change.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 280 and its Python in-place list contract. The Reference preserves the non-strict alternating inequalities, both source examples and explanation presence, all three constraints, and the source-native O(n) follow-up.

The protected app-local and native sources remain structurally aligned, and the immutable native source remains tied to verified submission 2064305374. The candidate differs only by the local rename from index to i; it is separate, inert, locally validated evidence and has not been submitted or represented as Accepted.

The legal 32/128/512-element tiers require a full adjacent-repair pass and retain a 16x span. The candidate passes at -0.03 relative exponent and 0.78x largest ratio; a correct insertion-sort-then-interleave control passes every output but fails only scaling at +1.26 and 190.63x.

The Approach now targets the candidate's i-based scan exactly, proves why each swap strengthens rather than breaks the preceding inequality, accounts for in-place linear work, and separates equality, short-input, multiset-preservation, and slower sorting alternatives.

The hash-bound Premium Reference remains verified against authenticated source evidence, preserving both examples in order and their explanation presence, all three constraints, the follow-up after Constraints, and the zero-visual structure.

coverage: Both authenticated source examples appear first, in source order, with their exact input arrays and displayed output facts.

The previous suite omitted source example 2, mislabeled an invented increasing array as a sample, and hid the descending correctness row; the replacement suite makes every correctness behavior visible and labels additions as trials.
The suite covers the minimum one-element length, minimum and maximum element values, two-element swap and no-swap paths, odd and even lengths, and the in-place None-return contract.
Already-valid, increasing, descending, all-equal, duplicate-heavy, and alternating-extreme arrays exercise both odd-position and even-position local repairs without requiring strict inequalities.
Every row uses the non-strict wiggle_sort validator, which checks the alternating inequalities and preservation of the input multiset instead of requiring one arbitrary permutation.

The protected source and inert candidate produced identical valid in-place results for all 21,844 arrays of lengths 1 through 7 over values 0 through 3, and all 12 authored expected arrangements were independently checked for wiggle order and multiset equality.
All 12 correctness cases are visible samples or trials; the unchanged 32-, 128-, and 512-element descending workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json.
